symptom: Upfront fare quotes have drifted upward against settled fares over recent months. No pipeline has failed, no alert has fired, and the schema has not changed. Nobody knows why.

root_cause.headline: Introduction of unrecognized vendor_id (7) into real-time data not seen in training data.
root_cause.change_description: A new vendor (7) began appearing in the data as of December 2024, introducing semantic drift due to the absence of this category in the model's training phase.
root_cause.mechanism: Vendor 7 inflates drift in trip_minutes and avg_speed_mph calculations due to missing category handling in is_vendor_myle derived feature, leading to upstream impact on revenue predictions.
root_cause.why_monitors_missed_it: All standard structural monitors (freshness, volume, nulls, schema) were silent as they don't track semantic changes. However, a unique count monitor did flag the appearance of a new category.

impact.estimator_note: did_* nets out the control model's advantage from having more and fresher training data, measured on segments with no encoding defect. Report did_attributable_dollars as the headline; it is the stricter of the two estimates.

root_cause.recommended_fix: Update model training pipeline to incorporate all active vendor_ids, including 7, and retrain the model.
proven: Segment 7 shows degenerate trip_minutes and avg_speed_mph with both metrics being zero consistently (Feature Drift Report).
trip_minutes derived from pickup_at and dropoff_at timestamps (Feature Context).
Anomalous increase in distinct values in March 2025 for both pickup_at and dropoff_at (Profile Over Time).
Profile of vendor_id shows the appearance of a new type in December 2024.
inferred: Vendor changes can introduce undisclosed categories leading to drift, reasoned through drift patterns and categorical shifts.
